8730b971e2: Extended notes: the path of the voice
b042fa9551: The waist and belly muscles contract, the diaphragm moves up, and air is pushed out of the lungs, through the trachea to the glottis, where it vibrates the vocal folds. The sound waves then resonate in the pharynx, mouth and nasal cavity, and finally the tongue, lips and teeth shape them into words. If any link tenses up, the whole path suffers.
c99fa196a3: Singing and speaking both come from the voice. The difference is that singing goes higher and wider, lasts longer and relies more on a steady supply of breath.
c51c3c6d8c: **Pitch**: hear the pitch clearly to sing it accurately. Being "tone-deaf" usually means the ears haven't been trained yet; the voice itself is fine. How to practise: play a note on the guitar, hum it once in your head, then sing it and check with a tuner app.
0daba778b6: **Tone**: how high or low you place the sound, how much resonance you use and how deeply you breathe all depend on your ears to tell. Recording yourself and listening back again and again is the most direct way to train your ear.
b9a384d5ea: **Sitting to play and sing**: sit on the front third of the chair with your pelvis settled, the guitar close to your body and the music stand at eye level. Guitarists tend to look down at the fretboard, and once the neck bends, the throat gets squeezed too. Practise the chords until you don't need to look at your hands before you start playing and singing.
7a9b1b027b: Extended notes: eight points of vocal care
723bdfa252: **Smoking and drinking**: smoke irritates the airways and alcohol makes the vocal folds swell with blood; avoid both before and after singing.
984fd04176: **Spicy food**: curry, hot and numbing dishes and strongly flavoured food easily irritate the throat.
9f663955a9: **Overusing the voice**: talking loudly at length and screaming are big no-nos; whispering also tenses the vocal folds.
4171753c8f: **Look after yourself**: pause intense practice when you have a cold, a sore throat or swollen vocal folds.
b593d04de5: **Where you sing**: smoky karaoke rooms, late nights and noise wear out the voice more than anything.
f897aa21fd: **Drink plenty of water**: 1,500 to 2,000 ml of warm water a day, a little at a time, keeps the vocal fold membranes moist so they vibrate freely.
96369895e7: **Eating before singing**: milk, chocolate and sweets tend to cause phlegm; avoid them for three hours before performing.
1b1a8615fd: **When you want to clear your throat**: swallow instead of coughing hard. If hoarseness lasts more than two weeks, see an ENT doctor.
4f256e921e: Extended notes: warm-up and breathing exercises
5155da0b42: **1. Warm-up** (top to bottom, then back the other way)
026899becf: Head and neck: open and close the mouth in an O shape to loosen the jaw; roll the neck, then let it hang and feel the throat muscles.
a60833158b: Shoulders and hands: roll the shoulders clockwise and anticlockwise and feel the chest muscles.
e0b9d90072: Upper back: lean the upper back forward and feel the upper belly.
274b9abf74: Lower back: bend the upper body forward and feel the lower belly.
aadad4ce1e: **2. Basic breathing exercises** (use a metronome: natural breathing and slow in slow out at 10 BPM, quick in slow out at 40 BPM, quick in quick out at 80 BPM)
b4411bb9d5: /s/ slow out, empty before the next breath
6d2f3a5234: The most widely used in songs
6f4229bb3e: In quick in, quick out, a noisy inhale means you're using too much throat; relax the throat and let the belly lead.
007fd973a1: **3. Using the main muscles** (4/4 time, one breath per quarter note)
fda280fbf9: **Belly strength**: make a breathy sound on /s/; after four bars your belly should feel tight.
840c72df9f: **Throat strength**: sing low notes on /hei/ to build control over low pitches.
c77f2968fb: **Combined workout**: on /hu/, alternate one bar of low notes with one bar of falsetto.
297bb40c35: **Quick in, slow out**: when the /s/ exhale runs out, press lightly on your belly with your hand, then breathe in quickly; breathing out on /i/ instead also trains the belly muscles.
0a4033dab8: **Quick in, hold, out**: after a full breath, hold it and count, then breathe out, counting a little longer each time.
ee5d39f62e: **Belly against the wall**: face a wall with your belly lightly touching it and watch it rise and fall as you breathe.
7c8b7c5cde: **Paper ping-pong** (pairs): one person holds a sheet of paper by the middle of the top edge and lets it hang; two people take turns blowing the lower half from either side and watch it swing.
5be64d4d3c: **Tissue on the wall**: put a single thin tissue on the wall, let go, and keep it from falling with a steady stream of air.
c637d37b3b: **Blowing paper**: hold a sheet of paper by the middle of the top edge and let it hang; blow the lower half with a steady breath and see whether it swings smoothly.
a2c8bb5bb5: Extended notes: using it in songs, and breath points
7d08f41db5: There are two kinds of breath point: a **full breath** between phrases, with time to fill right up, and a **catch breath (sneaked breath)** mid-line, topping up quickly in a half-beat gap. Mark breath points on the music first; if you look for air halfway through, line endings often go weak.
